description:
Measured 2026-09-14 (scratchpad 8b_probe/alloc_body.fz): two calls of a function whose body computes `x + 1 > 0` allocate 2 structs (struct_bytes 64) on interp and run; the same expression in a guard allocates 0, only because the guard evaluator bypasses Kernel `+` with an unchecked iadd. The struct is the `{value, failed}` pair: `fz_op_add_ii` returns it as a fixed C pair in two lanes, and it becomes a heap tuple when passed to `arithmetic_result/1` (`@spec arithmetic_result({t, boolean}) :: t`). enum_list_allocations pins the same thing as struct_allocs = 10 for ten `+`s.

Change: a typed operand pair on an arithmetic operator lowers to the instruction form that reports its failure (overflow flag; the zero test for div and rem), the failed lane feeds a branch, and `arithmetic_result` IS that branch, so no tuple exists at any point on any door; a cross-kind pair (atom plus integer) lowers to the constant failure. The interpreter delivers the pair to `arithmetic_result` as its two lanes, the way a fixed C pair already arrives.

Why now: the effects fact (allocates/fails) judges allocation on the lowered body. As `+/2` stands it allocates, so no guard could call it. This is a prerequisite of that fact, not a follow-on.

What goes away: the materialized pair; struct_allocs 10 -> 0 and struct_bytes 320 -> 0 in enum_list_allocations.

Proof (counts, not wall clock): heap-counter fixture where body `+` and guard `+` both show struct_allocs 0, three doors; enum_list_allocations golden moves only in those two counters; cross_kind_operators and the arithmetic oracle fixtures unchanged.
title: Arithmetic results ride in lanes: the {value, failed} pair is never a heap tuple
